fields.description:
Discovered while resolving item 3 of story 2127-348c-c41d-472e (probe resolved-status decision).

## Problem
Cloud's absence probe hardcodes `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = frozenset({'Resolved','Done','Cancelled'})` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/probe.py`. The DC side already sources its equivalent from config (`ReconcilerConfig.resolved_statuses`, `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`; consumed via `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py`). A Cloud tenant whose workflow uses non-standard resolved-status names (e.g. 'Closed', 'Complete', "Won't Do") has those issues MISCLASSIFIED as PRESENT_FILTERED instead of PRESENT_RESOLVED — with no way to fix it short of a code change.

## Decision
A runtime/config hook IS warranted for Cloud<->DC parity: Cloud should read a `jira.resolved_statuses` config key (defaulting to the current three names) the same way DC reads `reconciler.resolved_statuses`. This is already recorded as a repo-artifact comment at probe.py `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES`.

## Plan
1. `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`: add `resolved_statuses: list[str]` to the `JiraConfig` dataclass, defaulting via `field(default_factory=lambda: ["Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"])`, mirroring `ReconcilerConfig.resolved_statuses`. Register the coercer `"resolved_statuses": _as_str_list` under `_SECTIONS["jira"]` so the value is parsed from `[tool.rebar.jira]` and the `REBAR_JIRA_RESOLVED_STATUSES` env override is auto-derived (no canonical-name override needed).
2. `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/probe.py`: resolve the resolved-status set from `load_config().jira.resolved_statuses` at classify time, keeping module-level `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` as the fallback. Mirror DC's `settings.py` guard: fall back to the default when the configured list is EMPTY as well as unset or malformed (`ConfigError`) — bind `frozenset(configured) if configured else RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` inside a `try/except ConfigError`, since `_as_str_list` coerces `[]`/`[""]` to `[]` without raising. `classify_probe_response` binds the resolved set into the shared `jira_family` classifier. Update the DECISION comment to note the hook now exists.
3. `docs/config.md`: document the new `resolved_statuses` key in the `[tool.rebar.jira]` block.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `JiraConfig` exposes `resolved_statuses: list[str]` defaulting to `["Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"]`.
- [ ] The key is coerced from `[tool.rebar.jira]` via `_as_str_list`, with `REBAR_JIRA_RESOLVED_STATUSES` auto-derived as its env override.
- [ ] A tenant configuring `jira.resolved_statuses = ["Closed","Complete"]` classifies a "Closed" issue as PRESENT_RESOLVED.
- [ ] Under that same custom config, a "Done" issue (absent from the custom set) classifies as PRESENT_FILTERED, proving the configured set is consulted rather than merged with the default.
- [ ] With the key unset, a "Done"/"Resolved"/"Cancelled" issue still classifies as PRESENT_RESOLVED via the module-level default fallback, so a stock DIG tenant is unaffected.
- [ ] An explicitly empty configured list (`jira.resolved_statuses = []`) falls back to the module default rather than binding an empty set, mirroring DC's `settings.py` guard.
- [ ] A held-out test pins the custom-name PRESENT_RESOLVED behavior and the default fallback; mutation-checked RED/GREEN.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the probe/config test modules are green.
